Ukraine uses drones to deliver food to Russian-occupied Oleshky
KYIV, Sept 28 - Ukraine's military has used drones to deliver food and medicine to the Russian-occupied town of Oleshky, the governor of Ukraine's Kherson region said, as officials warn about a worsening humanitarian crisis.
Governor Oleksandr Prokudin said on Sunday that, in the latest operation, heavy-lift drones delivered about four tons of food and medical supplies to 100 locations across the town simultaneously.
Oleshky, a frontline town on the Dnipro River, which separates Russian and Ukrainian forces, has been under Russian occupation since 2022.
Prokudin said that close to 2,000 people, including about 50 children, were being held "hostage", without food, electricity and water, and accused Moscow's forces of preventing them from escaping the town.
Ukrainian officials have warned of the situation in Oleshky becoming more dire.
The UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine has said that residents have endured months of food shortages and "extremely limited" access to basic necessities.
Ukrainian human rights ombudsman Dmytro Lubinets told Ukrainian media this month that Russia had not agreed to Ukrainian proposals to allow civilians to evacuate from Oleshky.
"People in the temporarily occupied Oleshky are being deprived of the basic means of survival. Russia bears full responsibility for this humanitarian catastrophe and its consequences," Ukrainian Foreign Minister Andrii Sybiha said on Sunday.
The Kremlin said last week that Oleshky had critical problems with food and medicine supplies, but that Russia's military was working to resolve them. REUTERS

Europe’s Read of the Trump-Xi Summit
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
14:09:00 UTC
23:09:00 KST

The summit between U.S. President Donald Trump and Chinese President Xi Jinping achieved one central objective: stabilization. It did not resolve the China-U.S. rivalry but helped contain it, by restoring a more predictable framework for managing tensions over trade, technology, and geopolitics.
Its main concrete outcome was modest: a two-month extension, until January 2027, of the trade truce first agreed after the Trump-Xi meeting in Busan a year ago, when Washington lowered tariffs and Beijing suspended export controls on rare earths and other critical minerals.
The two sides also activated the China-U.S. Boards of Trade and Investment and mutual support for each other’s G20 and APEC presidencies. The message is clear: not genuine rapprochement, but more disciplined management of strategic competition.
Yet the summit’s most consequential exchanges may have taken place behind closed doors over Iran. The public readout was brief, but Trump pressed Xi over Chinese support for Tehran, while both leaders publicly agreed that Iran must not acquire a nuclear weapon.
For the world’s two largest economies, which together account for nearly half of global economic output, de-escalation makes strategic sense, though for different reasons. Both sides would like to use a period of relative stability to buy time to reduce vulnerabilities, strengthen resilience, and recalibrate economic dependencies.
Diplomatically, both leaders are also playing to domestic audiences. Trump is seeking tangible economic gains, from agricultural purchases to aircraft orders, consistent with his long-standing focus on reducing the U.S. trade deficit and addressing structural imbalances that have weakened American manufacturing. Xi, meanwhile, wants to show that Washington is treating China as an equal, while easing the economic pressure Washington has steadily increased toward Chinese companies. For Beijing, stability is economic as well as diplomatic: détente buys time to support a weak domestic economy increasingly reliant on external demand as consumption at home remains subdued.
The European Union was another important audience for the summit. Decisions taken in Washington and Beijing increasingly shape European trade, technology, energy, and security.
First, Brussels and major European capitals have a strong interest in stable China-U.S. relations, particularly at a time when instability in the Middle East is generating mounting economic pressures on Europe through higher energy costs, disrupted trade routes, inflationary pressures, and weaker industrial competitiveness.
Second, Europe fears becoming an adjustment variable in the China-U.S. strategic competition. Washington holds technological leverage; Beijing controls minerals and key manufacturing supply chains. Europe remains exposed to both. The question is whether the EU can turn its own economic weight into strategic agency rather than simply absorb the consequences of decisions taken elsewhere.
Consider trade relations. When China-U.S. trade tensions intensify, Chinese goods shut out of the American market are increasingly redirected toward Europe, raising fears of a deeper China shock. The automotive sector is already reshaping European perceptions of China, but the pressure extend well beyond card. The question is how many other industries will follow.
In 2025, the EU increasingly became China’s primary export destination and trade deficit with China reached nearly 360 billion euro, with Chinese exports to Europe almost double the value of EU exports to China. Additional U.S. restrictions on Chinese imports could deepen this imbalance further.
At the same time, any China-U.S. managed trade arrangement that redirects Chinese purchases toward American goods could come at the expense of European exporters. Europe therefore faces pressure in both directions, from trade diversion when tensions rise and from preferential bilateral deals when they ease. On the other side, if China-U.S. relations stabilize, Beijing has less incentive to make concessions to Brussels. Either way, Europe risks becoming the adjustment variable in China-U.S. competition: absorbing displaced Chinese production while bilateral deals between Washington and Beijing are struck largely over its head.
Third, like the United States, the EU remains heavily dependent on China for rare earths, permanent magnets, and critical minerals, essential for Europe’s green, digital, and defense industries. 98 percent of EU demand for rare earth magnets is met by Chinese imports. The Trump-Xi Busan agreement in October 2025 brought relief also to Europe by easing immediate supply pressures. The recent China-U.S. summit produced no major new breakthrough, only an agreement to keep working on shortages and shipment levels.
For Europe, this may preserve some near-term stability, but it does little to reduce the underlying vulnerability. There is still a risk that a bilateral China-U.S. accommodation could improve supply security for American companies without resolving Europe’s exposure. In response, Brussels is increasingly aligning with U.S.-led initiatives, such as Pax Silica, and its own Critical Raw Materials Act to diversify supply chains, though reducing dependence on China will require years of investment, industrial capacity building, and transatlantic coordination.
Fourth, artificial intelligence. The Trump-Xi meeting produced no binding agreement, although the two sides launched an AI dialogue and a channel to manage serious incidents. Disputes over advanced chip exports remain unresolved. Beijing has an interest in buying time to reduce its dependence on U.S. technology, without the added burden of new tariffs and restrictions on Chinese companies.
For the EU, the risk is that the rules of AI race are increasingly shaped in a China-U.S. channel where Brussels has little influence. In the meantime, Europe remains heavily reliant on American processors and cloud providers and Chinese supply chains. The EU produces less than 10 percent of global semiconductors. Brussels is responding with its Technology Sovereignty Package paired with the Chips Act 2.0 and the Cloud and AI Development Act that aim to triple European data center capacity within five to seven years. Both acts are still proposals, however, with binding law months or possibly years away.
Attention will now turn to the next EU-China Summit, which is slated to take place in Beijing on December 7, as Brussels is seeking tangible results from the EU-China Trade and Investment Council. The European Union has considerable leverage of its own, through its market, regulatory power, trade instruments, and industrial base. The question is whether is prepared and unified to use that leverage with China.
That is also why transatlantic coordination matters. Beijing benefits when U.S. and European positions diverge, while Washington has a clear interest in closer European alignment with its economic security approach. Europe’s strategic challenge is to avoid becoming merely the arena in which China-U.S. competition plays out and instead use its own agency to shape the terms of that competition.

Thailand's auto production surges 10.93 pct in August
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
22:02:28 CST
23:02:28 KST

BANGKOK, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Thailand's auto production increased in August, mainly due to higher output of electric vehicles (EVs) and export-oriented pickup trucks, data from the Federation of Thai Industries (FTI) showed on Monday.
Automakers produced 124,646 vehicles in Thailand last month, up 10.93 percent from a year earlier, accelerating from a 6.12 percent gain in July, according to the FTI.
The surge was attributed to notable growth in battery EV passenger car output and export-oriented pickup trucks, while combustion-engine passenger car output fell 20.51 percent, the FTI said in a statement.
For the first eight months of 2026, auto production rose 1.27 percent over the same period last year to 959,711 units, even as fuel-powered passenger cars sank 32.62 percent on lower export-oriented output, said FTI Automotive Industry Club spokesperson Surapong Paisitpattanapong.
Domestic auto sales jumped 25.59 percent year-on-year to 59,809 units in August, driven by higher deliveries of passenger battery EVs, which rose 113.29 percent and accounted for 32.97 percent of total sales, Surapong told a news conference.
Meanwhile, passenger cars with internal combustion engines dropped 17.04 percent, making up 13.33 percent of total sales, he said.
The Southeast Asian nation's finished car exports fell 2.04 percent from the year before to 69,724 units in August, as shipments to the Middle East fell 40.24 percent owing to the ongoing geopolitical conflict, he noted. ■

China Focus: China opens four high-speed rail lines, expanding national network
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
22:02:23 CST
23:02:23 KST

The first train of Yichang-Xingshan high-speed railway, G6888, departs from Xingshan Railway Station in Xingshan County, central China's Hubei Province, Sept. 28, 2026. The 101-kilometer Yichang-Xingshan high-speed railway officially entered service on Monday. The railway, with a designed speed of 350 kilometers per hour, is an important part of the country's high-speed rail network. (Photo by Zou Yuanjing/Xinhua)
BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China, home to the world's largest high-speed rail network, opened four major high-speed railway sections to traffic on Monday, improving transport links across several regions.
The new sections connect Xiong'an in Hebei Province with Shangqiu in Henan Province, Xi'an with Ankang in Shaanxi Province, Yichang with Xingshan in Hubei Province, and Harbin with Yichun in Heilongjiang Province.
Spanning northern, northwestern, central and northeastern China, the new lines will facilitate travel for residents, improve regional connectivity and support economic development.
In north China, the Xiong'an-Shangqiu section runs through Xiong'an New Area, Cangzhou, Hengshui and Xingtai in Hebei Province, Liaocheng in Shandong Province, Puyang in Henan Province, and Jining and Heze in Shandong Province before reaching Shangqiu in Henan Province, with the main line measuring 552 kilometers long.
"Once the section begins operations, the fastest journey from Xiong'an to Shangqiu will take just 2 hours and 27 minutes," said Han Yong, deputy director of the passenger transport center of China Railway Beijing Group Co., Ltd., adding that the route will further strengthen communications between Xiong'an New Area and China's vast northern and central markets.
In northwest China, the 171-km Xi'an-Ankang section crosses the Qinling Mountains, overcoming complex geological challenges while also prioritizing ecological protection. With a design speed of 350 km per hour, the train can travel between its two terminal stations in just 45 minutes.
Construction of the Yichang-Xingshan section in central China faced similar challenges, with the railway traversing the Daba Mountains through a 16.9-km-long deep-buried tunnel and a high-rise mega bridge.
The Yichang-Xingshan line connects China's two major high-speed railway arteries, namely the Shanghai-Chongqing-Chengdu high-speed railway along the Yangtze River and the Zhengzhou-Chongqing high-speed railway, and will unleash fresh development momentum along the Yangtze River Economic Belt, according to China Railway Wuhan Bureau Group Co., Ltd., its operator.
In northeast China, the 318-km Harbin-Yichun section is China's northernmost high-speed railway ever constructed. Its terminal, Yichun West Station, is located at 47 degrees north latitude, making it China's first high-speed railway station building constructed in a permafrost region, said Shi Qinwei, head of the Yichun West Station project at China Railway Construction Group Co., Ltd.
Linking Harbin, China's renowned winter destination in Heilongjiang Province with Yichun, the province's forest-enclosed haven for summer retreat, the route will cut the railway travel time between the two cities from about seven hours to roughly two hours, while extending China's modern high-speed rails to the lesser-tapped northern regions.
Opened shortly before the National Day holiday, the new railways are also expected to boost tourist flows between China's major cities along the route, as well as iconic attractions such as Yichang's Three Gorges Dam and Yichun's emerald forests.
China State Railway Group Co., Ltd., the country's railroad operator, is expecting some 284 million passenger trips during the Mid-Autumn Festival and National Day holiday period, which extends from Sept. 23 to October 8.
China is expanding and optimizing its high-speed rail network to better serve its booming domestic markets and industries.
By the end of 2025, the country's total operating railway mileage had reached 165,000 km, including more than 50,000 km of high-speed rail.
Fixed-asset investment in the railway sector totaled 511.8 billion yuan (about 75.9 billion U.S. dollars) in the first eight months of the year, up 1.5 percent year on year, according to China State Railway Group Co., Ltd.
Under national plans, China's high-speed rail network is projected to hit 70,000 km by 2035, with eight north-south vertical lines and eight east-west horizontal lines. Once complete, the network will connect major cities, city clusters and key economic zones throughout the country. ■

China finished the table tennis competition with six of the seven gold medals available, missing out only the men's team title. China also collected four silvers and one bronze, while Japan finished with one gold, three silvers and three bronzes. ■

JINAN, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- International Olympic Committee honorary president Thomas Bach called for greater dialogue between civilizations and cultures on Monday, highlighting the common ground between Confucian thought and the Olympic movement.
"You are deepening the dialogue between Confucian wisdom and the Olympic spirit," Bach said in a video address to the Nishan Forum on World Civilizations in Qufu, the birthplace of Confucius.
Bach recalled his visit to Qufu in 2023, saying the trip had allowed him to see firsthand the similarities between Confucian thought and Olympism.
"I have indeed very fond memories of my visit to the birthplace of Confucius a few years ago," Bach said. "It gave me the opportunity to discover firsthand how much Confucian thought and Olympism have in common."
Bach said Confucius' emphasis on developing both body and mind reflected an idea also found in the ancient Roman saying "Mens sana in corpore sano," meaning "a sound mind in a sound body."
"This same understanding is at the heart of Olympism," he said.
Bach said Pierre de Coubertin, founder of the IOC and reviver of the modern Olympic Games, viewed sport as being about more than physical competition, emphasizing education and values as well as building bridges and fostering understanding among nations and peoples.
"In our divided world, we need such dialogue between civilizations, people and cultures more than ever," Bach said.
He welcomed the return of the Nishan Forum's Sports and Culture Forum, first held in 2024, saying it continued to provide a platform to explore connections between Confucian thought and the Olympic spirit. ■

Economic Watch: Inbound travelers revel in Chinese goods, culture during Mid-Autumn holiday
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
22:02:10 CST
23:02:10 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- At Yuetan Park (Temple of the Moon) in Beijing, six-year-old Serena from Ireland pointed at a glowing panda lantern and tugged her father's sleeve. For her family, this Mid-Autumn Festival fair was not just a stop in their China trip, but a holiday event they could touch, taste and carry home.
"We came to admire the moon and lanterns, but the girls ended up with their pockets full of handmade crafts and local snacks," her father Marcus Rood said. Around this traditional Chinese festival of family reunion, more international visitors are coming to China and diving into experiences that go beyond just sightseeing.
The Mid-Autumn Festival falls on the 15th day of the eighth lunar month. During this year's Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, from Sept. 25 to 27, foreign nationals made 728,000 border crossings, up 37.7 percent year on year.
Among inbound foreign visitors, a total of 247,000 entered under visa-free policies, an increase of 32.7 percent from a year earlier, data from the National Immigration Administration showed.
In the bustling Dashilar area, a renowned tourist destination in downtown Beijing, time-honored shops and restaurants rolled out various Mid-Autumn cultural experiences. Overseas visitors flocked there to enjoy China's traditional song-and-dance performances and local delicacies.
For Celia Praetzas from Germany, an evening stroll turned into a shopping spree. Along a street decorated with giant installations blending Chinese pavilion architecture and heritage craft, she picked up low-sugar mooncakes, herbal tea and traditional Chinese health products.
Seeing so many families laughing together reminded Praetzas of hers. "I bought these for my parents, hoping they stay healthy and share in the joy of my trip here."
The Mid-Autumn Festival tells the story of home yet stirs a universal human yearning for belonging. "That's why the celebrations can touch foreign visitors," said Wang Yi, an associate professor at Tianjin University in north China.
Behind these scenes featuring overseas visitors soaking up China's festive atmosphere, is a sustained push to make the country more welcoming and easier to travel in.
In March, Chinese authorities released a package of measures to improve tourism services, including optimizing departure tax refund services, encouraging everyday service apps to offer multilingual versions, and further improving visa procedures.
These efforts are already paying off. Official data revealed that foreign nationals made nearly 61.29 million border crossings in the first eight months of 2026, up 19.5 percent year on year, while one of the leading mobile payment platform Weixin Pay reported that both the value and number of e-wallet transactions made by overseas users rose by more than 80 percent during the same period.
On Sept. 24, China's Ministry of Culture and Tourism announced plans to develop more travel experiences that combine traditional culture with modern life during 2026-2030, aimed at helping foreign visitors travel more conveniently, enjoy more comfortable stays, and gain a closer view of contemporary China.
Clutching a villager's ID card and breathing in the sweet aroma of local tea, Thai tourist Pam wandered through earthen courtyards and cave-like alleys in "See Minning," an immersive drama village in northwest China's Ningxia Hui Autonomous Region, where every few minutes she could run into another live scene.
Pam, who was visiting with her family during the Mid-Autumn Festival holiday, most enjoyed "Loess Cave," a story about villagers who once struggled with water shortages but now cherish a better life. "I was thrilled. It's hard to describe how amazing it is," she said.
The village has received almost 1,000 inbound visitors like Pam since it opened on July 1, and "Loess Cave," her favorite, now has an English version. Feng Xinxin, brand director of the village, said more plays will be translated into English as part of a regular international performance and exchange program.
"Inbound consumption by foreign visitors is shifting from products to immersive experiences, and thanks to the expanding visa-free policy, overseas tourists visit more often and tend to explore in greater depth, with varied and increasingly satisfying experiences," said Sun Jiashan, a researcher with the Central Institute of Socialism.
In July, China announced ambitious inbound tourism goals. The country's 2026-2030 tourism development plan proposes attracting 190 million inbound tourist visits a year by 2030, with annual inbound tourism spending exceeding 150 billion U.S. dollars.
As Dai Bin, president of China Tourism Academy, observed, tourism offers an immersive showcase of China's progress in manufacturing and services.
"Easier access to China for foreign visitors is not enough. We should provide better services to help them travel to more places, stay longer and have a good experience," Dai said. ■

Feature: Chinese artistic swimmer Guo makes a splash on Asian Games debut
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
22:01:58 CST
23:01:58 KST

NAGOYA, Japan, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- As the final notes faded over the rippling water, 18-year-old Guo Muye completed the last movement alongside his teammates. China remained atop the standings, and a gold medal crowned the teenager's Asian Games debut.
"It is very exciting. After all, this is my first time competing at such a major continental multi-sport event," Guo said after helping China win the artistic swimming team title on Monday.
The youngest and only male athlete on China's artistic swimming team at the Games, Guo competed in all three team routines over three days: the strength and grace of "Soul of the Terracotta Warriors," the agile movements inspired by "Black Myth: Wukong" and the philosophical storytelling of a new routine themed around "Time."
"I think I performed at the level I should have. My condition was even a little better than in regular training," he said.
Guo began swimming at age four. He and his twin brother, Guo Muxi, were later spotted by the Beijing artistic swimming team, setting him on a new path in the water.
International competition accelerated Guo's development. In 2025, he won one gold and three silvers at the World Aquatics Artistic Swimming World Cup Super Final before taking silver in the men's solo free at the World Championships in Singapore.
He joined China's senior national team in February and has since had to adapt to the demands of competing alongside more experienced teammates.
"My mindset has matured a lot, and my technique and ability have improved. But there is still a gap between me and the team's standards," Guo said. "I need to keep honing my skills and try to catch up with my older teammates."
Guo's emergence comes as men take on a growing role in artistic swimming. Male athletes were first allowed to compete in mixed duets at the World Championships in 2015, and World Aquatics later opened the Olympic team event to men, with up to two permitted on each team.
At the Aichi-Nagoya Asian Games, three of the five teams in the artistic swimming competition, China, Thailand and Kazakhstan, included male athletes.
China head coach Zhang Xiaohuan said the strength and explosiveness of male athletes can have a particular impact in lifts, difficult acrobatic elements and choreography.
But artistic swimming also demands flexibility, precision, synchronization and expressive ability, areas in which Guo acknowledges he still has room to improve.
"Flexibility training is difficult for me. I need to spend more time practicing," he said. "Train more and stretch my legs more."
As the youngest member of the team, Guo has also found support from his older teammates, who help him refine movements and adjust to new routines.
"After more than half a year of training together, he has become an inseparable part of the team," Zhang said. "Though he is the youngest, he has also become someone his older teammates can rely on."
With new routines and more difficult elements already on the training agenda, Guo is looking toward next year's World Championships, which will also serve as an Olympic qualifier.
Asked about his longer-term ambition, the teenager smiled shyly before giving a two-word answer.
"Olympic champion." ■

China Focus: China's BeiDou navigation system expands into diverse sectors amid tech convergence
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
22:01:38 CST
23:01:38 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- China is accelerating the integration of its BeiDou Navigation Satellite System (BDS) with frontier technologies, expanding its application from consumer devices to industrial operations and powering growth across sectors.
Integration with frontier technologies, such as 5G and 6G, artificial intelligence, remote sensing and low-Earth-orbit satellites, is unlocking new capabilities for BeiDou-enabled devices.
"BeiDou has established real-time centimeter-level positioning coverage across China and global high-precision positioning services with fast convergence," said Gou Ping, chairman of China Satellite Network Group Co., Ltd. "The system can support stable connectivity for billions of terminals, hundreds of millions of consumer users and millions of industrial users."
On the consumer end, more than 98 percent of smartphones sold in China now support BeiDou positioning, and over 100 million passenger vehicles are equipped with BeiDou onboard systems, according to an industry report released by the GNSS and LBS Association of China (GLAC).
Liu Zhenfei, chairman of Amap, Alibaba's mapping platform, said the company's AI-native agent -- described as the world's first built on map-based spatial intelligence -- relies on BeiDou's precise location and timing services.
The platform, now one of the world's largest civilian BeiDou service providers, makes approximately 1 trillion positioning requests per day, supporting a daily navigation distance of roughly 9 billion kilometers.
Beyond consumer applications, BeiDou is reshaping traditional industries. In Shanghai's suburban farmlands, more than 10,000 mu (about 667 hectares) of high-standard farmland have become a showcase for smart agriculture, with BeiDou-enabled machinery handling every step of rice cultivation -- from plowing to harvesting.
"The automatic navigation system for agricultural machinery, integrated with next-generation BeiDou positioning terminals, delivers more precise positioning and more stable signals," said Liu Bolin, an executive at a Shanghai-based tech firm.
According to data from the Ministry of Industry and Information Technology, by the end of 2025, cumulative shipments of domestically produced BeiDou-compatible chips and modules had neared 2.6 billion units, while the total installed base of BeiDou-enabled terminals had exceeded 2.2 billion.
By the end of 2025, BeiDou had penetrated key sectors such as transportation, energy, urban development and emergency relief, while expanding into emerging areas such as the low-altitude economy, marine economy, and cultural and sports events.
Buoyed by its domestic reach, BeiDou is accelerating its global footprint. As one of four global navigation satellite systems recognized by the United Nations, BeiDou-related products have been exported to more than 140 countries and regions.
Chinese companies have formed an overseas alliance of 40 enterprises, running short-message application tests in Indonesia and Malaysia and establishing cooperation hubs in Brazil and Kazakhstan.
The efforts underpin a broader industry shift from simple product exports to localized, integrated solutions, with Chinese BeiDou companies increasingly delivering turnkey packages to overseas markets.
"With more sectors adopting BeiDou and more companies joining the industry, we are confident the sector will break through the 1 trillion yuan mark," said Li Zhisong, vice president of the GLAC. Sustained technological advancement and mature business models would be essential to better serve socio-economic development, Li added. ■

====================================================================================================

FAO report urges large-scale forest, landscape restoration to boost food security
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
22:01:37 CST
23:01:37 KST

ROME, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- Large-scale restoration of forests and landscapes is a cost-effective way to address food security, biodiversity and climate challenges, according to a report released Monday by the Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations (FAO).
The 2026 edition of the FAO's flagship State of the World's Forests report, released during the 28th Session of the Committee on Forestry, calls for greater investment, inclusive governance and sustained political commitment to scale up restoration efforts.
Forests cover about 4.14 billion hectares, or 32 percent of the world's land area, and store an estimated 714 gigatons of carbon. They also support food security and livelihoods for nearly one-third of the global population, according to the report.
However, about 489 million hectares of forest were lost to deforestation between 1990 and 2025, while more than 460 million hectares of forests are degraded worldwide. An estimated 1.56 billion hectares of land are degraded, driven by population growth, land-use change and growing demand for natural resources.
The report estimated that failing to restore degraded ecosystems costs the global economy between 878 billion U.S. dollars and 6.3 trillion dollars annually. By contrast, restoring more than 1 billion hectares of degraded land could generate 1.8 trillion dollars in annual benefits through improved biodiversity, water regulation and soil health.
FAO Director-General QU Dongyu said forest and landscape restoration is "more than an environmental priority," describing it as a strategic investment in resilient agrifood systems and rural development.
The report identified four priorities for expanding restoration: strengthening people's rights and participation, adopting landscape-scale approaches, mobilizing long-term financing, and improving policies, laws and institutions.
Governments in 91 countries and areas have pledged more than 190 million hectares for forest restoration, the report said. It cited China's Three-North Shelterbelt Program, the Great Green Wall initiative in Africa's Sahara and Sahel region, and the Trinational Atlantic Forest Pact in South America as examples of large-scale restoration efforts. ■

Emphasizing workplace safety in key industries and fields, Li urged efforts to strengthen whole-chain safety supervision of fireworks and firecrackers, carry out special rectification of coastal and river vessel enterprises, and enhance tourism and traffic safety management around the National Day holiday.
He also underscored accident prevention in sectors including hazardous chemicals, industry and trade, and construction.
The premier urged enterprises to comprehensively enhance workplace safety by accelerating the phase-out of outdated equipment and technological upgrading, and improving safety management systems.
Stressing the importance of raising public awareness of workplace safety laws and knowledge, and fostering a safety culture, Li also urged efforts in disaster prevention, mitigation and relief, including monitoring and early warning, hazard inspection, duty shifts, and improving emergency plans so as to minimize disaster losses. ■

China Focus: Chinese Academy of Sciences sets priorities for sci-tech breakthroughs in its five-year plan
China
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
22:01:35 CST
23:01:35 KST

BEIJING, Sept. 28 (Xinhua) -- The Chinese Academy of Sciences (CAS) has released its development plan for the 15th Five-Year Plan period (2026-2030), setting priority directions for sci-tech breakthroughs in three major fields: basic research, strategic high technologies and sustainable development.
The plan defines the strategic priorities guiding the academy's sci-tech work in the coming years, and calls for stronger foundational sci-tech capabilities and better coordination of the regional layout of sci-tech research.
It designates the academy's important priority fields, strategic high-technology fields, sustainable development fields, as well as basic frontier and interdisciplinary fields in its sci-tech innovation layout, targeting to cultivate a batch of key development directions and make the layout more strategic, forward-looking and systematic.
According to the plan, the important priority fields include integrated circuits, AI, quantum technology, life sciences and biotechnology, brain-computer interfaces, controlled nuclear fusion, among others.
The strategic high-technology fields cover optoelectronics, space, information, ocean, energy and materials. Its sustainable development fields include agriculture, Earth and resources, atmosphere, ocean and ecological environment. As for the basic frontier and interdisciplinary fields, the plan lists the mathematics, physics, chemistry, biology, astronomy and geoscience.
To coordinate and optimize the regional sci-tech layout, the plan will accelerate the construction of a tiered regional layout system as an endeavor to provide systematic sci-tech support for the country's major regional strategies.
In this system, Beijing (the Beijing-Tianjin-Hebei region), Shanghai (the Yangtze River Delta) and the Guangdong-Hong Kong-Macao Greater Bay Area are considered as the strategic highlands, and Hefei, Chengdu-Chongqing, Wuhan and Xi'an as strategic pivots, with a number of key regions as strategic nodes.
The plan also pledges to step up AI-enabled scientific research. It aims to leverage the academy's strengths in mathematics, computer science, control science, and scientific data to enhance the development of new sci-tech infrastructure. This includes the ScienceOne Omni foundation model, intelligent scientist systems, a sci-tech corpus, and a scientific data center. The goal is to accelerate efficient, collaborative support for research.
The plan will actively promote the digital, networked and intelligent iterative upgrading of facilities and platforms such as major national sci-tech infrastructure as well as national field scientific observation and research stations.
It will also step up efforts to collect and integrate data, unify standards and specifications, and strengthen data security. At the same time, it aims to improve data fusion, interoperability, and application, providing strong support for scientific research in key areas and the implementation of major sci-tech projects.
Guided by the needs of building a modern industrial system, the plan will focus on important fields, key regions and major projects, and adopt a two-pronged approach that combines supply-side advances in sci-tech innovation with demand-side pull from industry, so as to accelerate the transformation of sci-tech achievements into real productivity.
Aiming to build a world-class research institution, the plan also outlines reform and development tasks in areas including integrated development of education, science and technology and talent, construction of a national science and technology think tank, reform and management innovation of research organizations, transfer and application of sci-tech achievements, and international sci-tech exchanges and cooperation. ■

Neuroscientists shed light on how the brain juggles talking and listening during real conversation
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
14:00:44 UTC
23:00:44 KST

When humans engage in a conversation, the brain must seamlessly process both the words they want to say and the sentences they are hearing. A new study reveals that the brain uses shared neural codes for speaking and listening during short verbal exchanges, but relies on distinct timing networks to process longer, overarching ideas. These findings, published in Nature Human Behaviour, help map how the brain navigates the back-and-forth demands of natural social interaction.
Conversation is a highly dynamic activity that requires people to understand context, anticipate responses, and build a cohesive narrative together. To do this, the human brain must integrate language across multiple timescales. This ranges from the immediate processing of individual words to the broader comprehension of entire paragraphs and concepts.
For decades, researchers have studied how the brain processes language by having participants listen to isolated sentences or read long narratives. These past experiments established that the brain organizes language hierarchically. However, it was not entirely known how the brain handles the two-way street of spontaneous, real-time conversation.
Neuroscientists sought to determine whether the brain uses the exact same linguistic representations for generating speech and comprehending speech, or if it keeps those processes separated. A research team led by Masahiro Yamashita and Shinji Nishimoto at Osaka University and the National Institute of Information and Communications Technology in Japan set out to answer this question. They designed a study to map out how brain activity shifts depending on whether a person is talking or listening, and how much previous context they are factoring in.
The researchers recruited eight native Japanese speakers for a small study involving brain imaging. Each participant lay inside a functional magnetic resonance imaging scanner, a machine that tracks blood flow in the brain to measure neural activity. While inside the scanner, the participants engaged in unscripted, natural conversations with an experimenter through a microphone and earphones. They discussed casual topics, such as their favorite classes and personal introductions, for roughly three hours each.
To translate the messy, spontaneous nature of human speech into a format the researchers could analyze, they turned to a large language model. This artificial intelligence tool, based on the GPT architecture, was trained to predict language patterns by processing massive amounts of text. The researchers fed the transcripts of the participants’ conversations into the artificial intelligence to extract mathematical representations of the text’s meaning, known as contextual embeddings. They did this for different lengths of time, analyzing context windows that lasted anywhere from one second to thirty-two seconds.
The team then built computer models to predict the brain activity of the participants based on the artificial intelligence’s mathematical breakdown of the conversations. They first tested a model that treated speaking and listening as one shared pool of meaning. The results showed that when looking at short timescales of one to four seconds, the brain shares its linguistic representations regardless of whether a person is talking or listening. The neural codes used for formulating a quick thought and hearing a brief sentence overlapped in the prefrontal, temporal, and parietal cortices.
However, the researchers found a different pattern when examining longer stretches of conversation. When looking at context windows of sixteen to thirty-two seconds, the shared representations scattered across the brain. The patterns varied widely from person to person, occasionally reaching regions associated with guessing the thoughts of others and recalling memories. This suggests that while the brain uses a universal system to process immediate words, individuals use personalized strategies to integrate overarching social context and long-term conversation history.
Next, the researchers isolated the brain activity uniquely tied to just speaking or just listening. They discovered an opposing timescale preference for each action. The brain areas dedicated to producing speech were most active when processing short-term context. Conversely, the brain areas dedicated to understanding the experimenter’s speech were most active when processing long-term context spanning multiple sentences.
This division aligns with the specific demands of each task. Producing speech requires a person to react quickly to what the other person just said, planning words and sentence structures on the fly. Listening requires a person to hold onto information over time to build a complete mental model of what their conversational partner means.
The researchers also looked for brain regions that responded robustly to both speaking and listening, but in completely independent ways. They identified specific bimodal zones that peaked in activity only when factoring in longer context lengths of eight seconds or more. These areas encoded meaning for both tasks but did not share the exact same neural patterns, pointing to specialized regions that help individuals separate their own perspectives from those of their conversation partners. To navigate a dialogue, the brain must keep track of who knows what, and these bimodal zones likely support that cognitive juggling.
Finally, the team used a statistical technique to break down the specific types of words that drove the strongest brain responses at short timescales. They found that conversational fillers and short confirmations, such as “yeah” or “uh,” evoked distinct neural patterns. These tiny words require very little cognitive effort to say, but they act as social glue to maintain the flow of dialogue. The brain appears to have dedicated neural tuning for these interactive words, separating them from highly logical or factual statements.
Because this was a small study involving only eight people, the findings represent a narrow slice of the population. The researchers noted that they did not use functional localizer tasks, which are preliminary tests used to outline established brain networks, such as the regions responsible for mentalizing what other people are thinking. Without these preliminary tests, the team could not definitively map their results onto precisely defined cognitive networks. Future research with larger groups and additional mapping techniques will be needed to confirm exactly which distinct brain networks manage these conversational timelines.
The study, “Conversational content is organized across multiple timescales in the brain,” was authored by Masahiro Yamashita, Rieko Kubo, and Shinji Nishimoto.

In his nightly video address, Zelenskiy said Ukraine was still having difficulty countering faster, high-flying Russian jet-powered drones -- 90 of 120 drones fired on Ukraine were jet propelled, rather than propeller-driven, and the interception rate was 57%.

In Germany, law enforcement and intelligence agencies are searching for weapons caches that Russian agents may have prepared for sabotage operations at defense facilities.

German intelligence agencies received information from foreign intelligence about the possible transport of weapons from Serbia to Germany.
The weapons may have been intended for sabotage against a defense facility in Bavaria, where many defense companies producing weapons for Ukraine are located.
On June 27, German border guards stopped a truck that had entered the country from Austria. They found specially equipped hidden compartments inside, but they were empty.
Investigators are now examining whether these weapons could have entered Germany earlier and been hidden elsewhere.
Investigators suspect that the weapons may have been unloaded earlier and hidden somewhere in Germany. Law enforcement officials are therefore trying to locate a possible hiding place.
According to BILD, the investigation is also looking into a possible connection between this case and Russian intelligence services. German security agencies have not yet disclosed details of the investigation.
The increased activity of Russian intelligence services in Germany is not new and is growing rapidly. The country is seeing both an increase in arson attacks on German military equipment—such as on September 26, 2026, when three Bundeswehr trucks were burned at the MAN facility near Magdeburg—and attempts to set fire to defense companies.
On the night of September 3, incendiary devices were thrown from a moving vehicle onto a construction site near the companies’ headquarters.
While inspecting the scene, law enforcement officers found another incendiary device that had not detonated. It was rendered harmless.
Subsequently, law enforcement officers detained two Bulgarian citizens—a 28-year-old woman and a 38-year-old man—at a gas station. They may have been part of a group linked to Russian military intelligence operating out of Slovakia.
Meanwhile, the German Ministry of the Interior intends to develop a set of measures to counter Russian sabotage, including cyberattacks.
These measures are intended to ensure complete protection against drones in the airspace above critical infrastructure, airports, train stations, and the government district of the capital. In addition to interception, their tasks also include neutralizing explosive devices.
This followed the discovery on the night of August 5 of a drone equipped with explosives near a Ukrainian An-124 Ruslan transport aircraft. On September 1, Germany officially accused Russia.

Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
13:37:05 UTC
22:37:05 KST

Scientists just discovered what coffee really does to your gut and brain
- Date:
- September 28, 2026
- Source:
- University College Cork
- Summary:
- A new study suggests coffee may influence mood and brain function by changing the activity of microbes in the gut. Both caffeinated and decaf coffee were linked to lower stress, depression, and impulsivity, while also producing measurable changes in gut bacteria and metabolites. Decaf was associated with better learning and memory, while caffeinated coffee appeared to reduce anxiety and improve attention.
- Share:
Coffee may affect far more than alertness. New research suggests that both regular and decaffeinated coffee can alter the gut microbiome and may influence mood, stress, memory, and attention through the gut brain connection.
Scientists at APC Microbiome Ireland, a research center at University College Cork, investigated in detail how coffee may influence communication between the digestive system and the brain.
The study published in Nature Communications and sponsored by the Institute for Scientific Information on Coffee (ISIC), found that both caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee were associated with changes in the gut microbiome as well as differences in mood and stress.
How Coffee May Affect the Gut-Brain Connection
Scientists have long studied coffee for possible effects on digestion, mood, and overall health, but exactly how these effects arise has remained less clear.
The new research focused on the microbiota-gut-brain axis, the two-way communication system linking microorganisms in the digestive tract with the brain. Signals can travel between the gut and brain through immune activity, hormones, nerves, and chemical compounds produced by microbes.
Researchers examined 31 regular coffee drinkers and 31 people who did not normally drink coffee. Participants completed psychological assessments and kept records of caffeine intake and diet. Researchers also collected stool and urine samples to track changes in gut microbes, metabolism, mood, and perceived stress.
For the study, 'Coffee drinkers' were set as those who regularly consume 3-5 cups of coffee a day, defined by the European Food Safety Authority (EFSA) as a safe and moderate amount for most people.
What Happened When Coffee Was Removed
The regular coffee drinkers first stopped consuming coffee for two weeks. During that period, participants repeatedly completed psychological assessments and provided stool and urine samples.
When coffee drinkers stopped drinking coffee, researchers observed substantial shifts in their gut metabolite profiles compared with people who did not normally consume coffee. Metabolites are small molecules produced or altered during metabolism, including compounds created by gut microbes as they process food and other substances.
Coffee was then reintroduced without participants knowing whether they were receiving caffeinated or decaffeinated coffee. Half received decaf, while the other half received caffeinated coffee.
After coffee returned to their diets, both groups reported lower perceived stress, depression and impulsivity scores. The findings suggest that some of coffee's effects on mood may not depend entirely on caffeine.
Coffee Was Linked to Changes in Gut Bacteria
Researchers also found differences in several types of gut bacteria.
Bacteria, such as 'Eggertella sp.' or 'Cryptobacterium curtum', were more abundant among coffee drinkers than non-coffee drinkers. 'Eggertella sp' is thought to contribute to acid secretion in the stomach and intestines, while 'Cryptobacterium curtum' may participate in bile acid production.
Both processes could potentially help create an intestinal environment that discourages certain harmful bacteria and infections.
Researchers also observed higher levels of 'Firmicutes' bacteria, a broad group of microbes that has previously been associated with positive emotions in females.
Decaf and Caffeinated Coffee Showed Different Effects
One of the most intriguing findings was that caffeinated and decaffeinated coffee did not appear to affect participants in exactly the same way.
Improved learning and memory were observed only among participants drinking decaffeinated coffee. That finding suggests that substances other than caffeine may contribute to some of coffee's effects on cognition.
Coffee contains thousands of chemical compounds, including polyphenols. These plant derived substances can act as antioxidants and can also interact with gut microbes, potentially influencing metabolism and other biological processes.
Caffeinated coffee, meanwhile, was associated with reduced feelings of anxiety as well as improved vigilance and attention. Caffeine was also linked to a reduced risk of inflammation.
Because the study involved a relatively small number of participants, the findings do not establish that coffee directly causes these changes in mood, cognition, or gut health. However, they provide new clues about the biological pathways that could help explain associations reported in earlier coffee research.
Coffee Is More Than Caffeine
Corresponding author of the study, Professor John Cryan, Principal Investigator at APC Microbiome Ireland, University College Cork, commented: "Public interest in gut health has risen hugely. The relationship between digestive and mental health is also increasingly being better understood, but the mechanisms behind coffee's effects on this gut-brain axis have remained unclear.
"Our findings reveal the microbiome and neurological responses to coffee, as well as their potential long-term benefits for a healthier microbiome. Coffee may modify what microbes do collectively, and what metabolites they use. As the public continues to think about dietary changes for the right digestive balance, coffee has the potential to also be harnessed as a further intervention as part of a healthy balanced diet."
The findings add to growing evidence that coffee should not be viewed simply as a source of caffeine. Its many other components may interact with the microbiome, metabolism, and nervous system in different ways.
"Coffee is more than just caffeine -- it's a complex dietary factor that interacts with our gut microbes, our metabolism, and even our emotional well-being," said Professor Cryan. "Our findings suggest that coffee, whether caffeinated or decaffeinated, can influence health in distinct but complementary ways."

Lee Asks Trump to Help Revive North Korea Talks During New York Trip
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
13:36:00 UTC
22:36:00 KST

South Korean President Lee Jae-myung asked U.S. President Donald Trump to help restart talks between the United States and North Korea in an unannounced meeting on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly on September 22, according to the Blue House, the presidential office of South Korea. The Blue House also said that Trump reaffirmed his willingness to engage with North Korean leader Kim Jong Un.
The talks were arranged at the last minute. In the 30-minute meeting. Lee asked Trump to create a breakthrough amid almost no direct contact between the two Koreas. The two leaders also agreed to communicate closely as “peacemakers and pacemakers,” according to the Blue House.
Trump has been courting Kim since August, when he scaled back a major joint military exercise with South Korea. A day later, he said Kim had responded to his request for dialogue, calling the exchange very positive without offering details. Trump has since signaled he hopes to meet Kim before the end of the year – possibly during the Asia-Pacific Economic Cooperation (APEC) summit in Shenzhen, China, this November.
Yet North Korea denied any direct contact in a statement by Kim Yo Jong, the powerful sister of Kim Jong Un. She described the relationship between the two leaders as “excellent” while insisting that Washington had not changed its hostile policy. She also said North Korea was not impressed by the reduction in scale of the South Korea-U.S. joint exercises, calling it “unworthy of comment.”
Lee had made the case for reopening dialogue earlier on September 22 in an address to the General Assembly. In the speech, Lee said he hoped to see the long-suspended dialogue between North Korea and the United States resume without delay. He also added that his administration would lay the groundwork for talks among the parties aimed at formally ending the Korean War.
On North Korean weapons, Lee outlined a sequence that would begin with a halt to further advances in North Korean nuclear and missile capabilities. Then reductions would follow over the medium term, with the ultimate goal of a Korean Peninsula free of nuclear weapons. Lee credited Trump with creating a hard-won opportunity for change and pledged to act as a “pacemaker” for peace.
The speech came a day after the foreign ministers of South Korea, the U.S., and Japan reaffirmed their commitment to the complete denuclearization of North Korea in a joint statement issued on the sidelines of the same General Assembly session. The statement also urged Pyongyang to return to talks.
North Korean Foreign Minister Choe Son Hui denounced the joint statement on September 24, declaring in a message carried by state media that the will of her country to keep nuclear weapons through all ages was “irreversible.”
Beyond North Korea, in their brief meeting Lee and Trump took up alliance issues such as nuclear-powered submarines and the transfer of wartime operational control of South Korean forces from the U.S. Rights to enrich uranium and reprocess spent nuclear fuel, along with shipbuilding cooperation, also came up. Both leaders also welcomed progress on investment projects between the two countries. The Industry Ministry had briefed lawmakers on a $22.3 billion gas-fired power plant in Texas, which Seoul confirmed as the first project under a $200 billion strategic investment package. Under the trade deal, South Korea has pledged to invest $350 billion in the United States, including $150 billion set aside for shipbuilding.
While in New York, Lee also met U.N. Secretary-General Antonio Guterres to review Korean Peninsula issues and cooperation between South Korea and the United Nations. In a separate meeting, he held talks with Australian Prime Minister Anthony Albanese on energy cooperation amid disruptions linked to the Strait of Hormuz.
On September 23, Lee addressed the Korea Investment Summit in New York. He pledged to double semiconductor production capacity within five years and pointed to the shipbuilding cooperation covered in his meeting with Trump the day before.
Meanwhile, North Korea has said it tested a new weapon on September 20. That day, the South Korean military detected two short-range ballistic missile launches and assessed their flight distances at about 450 and 600 kilometers. Photos released by North Korea, however, showed a flight distance of 908.2 kilometers.
The North Korean delegation skipped the General Assembly address delivered by Lee. Two North Korean diplomats had attended the speech given by Trump earlier that day.
The U.N. General Assembly also overlapped with a summit between Trump and Chinese leader Xi Jinping in Washington, during the first visit to the U.S. capital by Xi in more than a decade. U.S. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent said the two sides agreed to extend their trade truce by two months, to January 10. The White House later said China and the United States had reached consensus on recommendations for more favorable tariff treatment for $30 billion of non-sensitive goods in each direction.
Each side also referred to the Korean Peninsula in its account of the talks. According to Washington, the two leaders discussed global concerns including Russia, North Korea, and Iran. Chinese state media reported that the leaders exchanged views on the Korean Peninsula, the Middle East, and the war in Ukraine. Neither side gave details of what was said about North Korea.
After his trip to New York, Lee paid a state visit to Mexico. Lee and Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum adopted a joint action plan for 2026 to 2030 and signed 17 cooperation documents covering areas from trade and critical minerals to aerospace and defense.

Punjab's election drug debate has old players in new roles: BJP, Congress attack as AAP defends its record
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
13:31:57 UTC
22:31:57 KST

NEW DELHI: "The sarpanch is also responsible for my death. I had questioned Cheema about drugs. My son takes drugs. My house was sold. I don't have anything and finally now I have consumed poison. The problem of drugs has not been solved anywhere in Punjab."Those were among the last recorded words of Gulzar Singh, a 47-year-old Dalit man from Dirba in Sangrur district, before his death. His family alleged that he had been pushed to the edge after questioning Punjab finance minister Harpal Singh Cheema about the easy availability of drugs in the area.Gulzar died, but his words reverberated across poll-bound Punjab. The BJP, Congress and Shiromani Akali Dal trained their guns on the Bhagwant Mann government, accusing it of failing to control the drug menace. AAP hit back, questioning their own records in power.Drugs have shadowed election after election in the state. Captain Amarinder Singh went into the 2017 polls promising to break the backbone of the drug trade within four weeks. Five years later, AAP sought votes with its own promise of eliminating the menace within months.
Now, with Punjab headed for another assembly election in 2027, drugs are again moving to the centre of the conversation.Only the roles have changed.AAP, which once attacked Congress and the SAD-BJP government from the outside, now has nearly five years in office to defend. Congress wants to use AAP's old promises against it. And the BJP, still trying to expand its footprint in Punjab, has launched perhaps its biggest statewide campaign yet around the issue.
BJP takes the drug battle on the road
Leading the opposition charge is the BJP, which has the weakest presence in the state as of now, but is making the strongest pitch for power.The Punjab BJP, on September 18, launched its 13-day 'Nasha Mukt Yatra' to turn its anti-drug campaign into a statewide political roadshow ahead of the 2027 assembly elections. The party divided its campaign into four yatras covering nearly 4,000 km and all 117 assembly constituencies.The campaign will end on September 30, with Union home minister Amit Shah likely to address the concluding rally. All the top BJP leaders including Union ministers and party chief ministers from other states have joined the campaign against drugs in Punjab.
BJP leader Anurag Thakur said the state has to be made 'Aam Aadmi Party Mukt' for turning it into 'Nasha Mukt'
Yet the BJP has a political history to answer for too. For 10 years, from 2007 to 2017, it shared power with the Shiromani Akali Dal, the period AAP repeatedly points to whenever its record on drugs is questioned.
From four weeks to three months: Punjab's many deadlines
Ahead of the 2017 election, Amarinder Singh's four-week promise became one of the defining messages of the Congress campaign. He later clarified that his pledge was about breaking the backbone of the drug supply chain rather than completely eliminating every trace of drugs within a month.By 2022, the roles had changed. AAP was the challenger and Arvind Kejriwal and other party leaders promised quick action, speaking of tackling the menace within three to four months of forming the government.The BJP has done its homework well. It knows that the drug menace in Punjab is deep-rooted and hence has sought a timeframe of two years to eradicate it. However, Union minister Shivraj Singh Chouhan has claimed that the BJP will destroy and eliminate the entire drug network within six months if voted to power in the state.Therein lies Punjab's problem: Congress cannot remind AAP about its three-month promise without being reminded of its own four-week vow. BJP cannot attack AAP without being taken back to its decade in government with SAD.Almost every party pointing fingers today has a past of its own to explain.
Congress, SAD join the attack
The Congress narrative on the drug menace seems to have been lost in the face of BJP’s high-decibel anti-drug campaign. The party, which for a long time was struggling to set its own house in order amid infighting, has done little till now to capitalise on the alleged failures of the AAP government to tackle the drug menace.The first big Congress show on the ground was only after Sachin Pilot took charge as state incharge and managed to get the rival state unit factions on one stage to protest against Punjab minister Cheema over the suicide of Gulzar.
Punjab finance minister blamed BJP-SAD for the drug menace in the state,
Pilot said: “If someone raises their voice against drugs, they face such attacks. I believe the government can go to any extent to suppress and conceal these voices. There are two sets of laws in the country, one for ministers and another for the common man. This cannot go on. I feel the government is completely on the back foot regarding the issue of drugs.”He then turned to AAP's pre-2022 promise: “The Aam Aadmi Party had promised in Punjab that they would eliminate the drug menace within three months of forming the government. They stand completely exposed. I sense a stir for change in Punjab, and change will happen.”Leader of opposition Partap Singh Bajwa has blamed both the AAP-led state government and the BJP-led Union government for turning the state's drug crisis into a political blame game instead of dismantling the drug supply chain.“Bhagwant Mann cannot wash his hands of responsibility by talking about cross-border, the BSF and Mundra Port. At the same time, the BJP cannot absolve itself by blaming Punjab while the international border, ports and the national drug-trafficking network fall within areas where the Union government has a critical responsibility. Punjab's youth need action, not a Mann-Modi blame-game,” Bajwa said.
Channi hits out at AAP govt
The Congress challenge is daunting. While on the one hand it has to target the AAP government’s failures, on the other, it also has to prevent the BJP from running away with the anti-drug fight initiative.SAD faces much the same problem. Bikram Singh Majithia recently took a jibe at the Punjab government when he said: “Under AAP's regime, delivery of drugs is faster than that of food.”Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal has also appealed to women in Punjab to unite and launch an ‘andolan’ to free the state from the drug menace, including through ‘thikri pehra’, a community policing practice in which people guard their localities during emergencies.
Bathinda MP Harsimrat Kaur Badal has appealed to women in Punjab to unite and launch an 'andolan'
AAP hits back: What about the years before 2022?
AAP's response is to ask its rivals to look backwards before judging the Mann government.Punjab minister Cheema, who is at the centre of the row over Gulzar’s suicide, shifted the blame to the BJP and the SAD.“The BJP should look at its own record. The drug menace intensified during the 10 years of the SAD-BJP government from 2007 to 2017. It was during that period that terms such as 'chitta' and 'smack' became widely associated with Punjab, with countless young lives being destroyed by addiction,” Cheema said.Countering the BJP offensive, AAP national convenor Arvind Kejriwal has alleged that the majority of narcotics entering the country originate from Bharatiya Janata Party-ruled states and major maritime entry points controlled by the Centre.Kejriwal alleged: “Today, 80% of the drugs are coming from BJP-ruled states - Gujarat, Rajasthan, Haryana, UP, Delhi. Has the BJP failed to stop the drug trade in its own states, or does it not want to stop it? Their government has been in power in Gujarat for thirty years, and the highest drug trade is there. Drugs enter India through Mundra Port, and stopping that is the responsibility of the central BJP government.”Bhagwant Mann, meanwhile, has launched the ‘Soorma’ campaign to honour drug-rehabilitated people with specially crafted ‘Soorma’ rings and T-shirts. The chief minister said the initiative aimed to transform recovered drug victims into “Ambassadors of Hope”, who will lead the fight against addiction at the grassroots.
Beyond the blame game, what do numbers say
The Mann government has numbers with which to defend itself.Punjab Police says its ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’ campaign has resulted in tens of thousands of cases and arrests. More recent state figures put the tally since March 2025 at 61,824 FIRs, 81,433 arrests and 3,918 kg of heroin seized.AAP presents the numbers as evidence that the state machinery is finally going hard after the networks. Its opponents turn the argument around: if such large quantities are still being seized and so many people are still being arrested, how deeply rooted does the trade remain?High seizures can show a crackdown is working but they can also show the scale of the problem being confronted.The government says its strategy now goes beyond policing. It has expanded treatment and rehabilitation under ‘Yudh Nashean Virudh’, with 547 OOAT centres, 219 de-addiction centres and 91 rehabilitation centres, besides programmes involving schools and local communities.
For AAP, this forms the other half of its defence: the battle against drugs cannot be measured only through FIRs and seizures but also through treatment and rehabilitation.
Punjab has seen this cycle before
In 2017, anger over drugs was directed largely at the SAD-BJP government and Congress promised quick action. By 2022, Congress was on the defensive and AAP used the same issue to argue that Punjab's traditional parties had failed. In 2027, AAP is the incumbent being asked many of the questions it once asked others.The slogans have changed and the roles have reversed, but the question has survived different governments and different deadlines: after so many promises to make Punjab drug-free, why is the state heading into yet another election talking about the same problem?

Xi Jinping demands ‘safer’ China as Communist Party prepares for leadership reshuffle
The directive signals Xi is pivoting back to the domestic agenda following his summit with Donald Trump in Washington
In a written directive relayed at a high-level meeting, Xi said the security and law enforcement apparatus must advance the “Peaceful China Initiative to a higher level” to ensure “steady and sustained progress in China’s modernisation”. Russia hammers Ukraine's capital with major daytime drone strike
Unknown
Unknown Publisher
2026-09-28
13:26:02 UTC
22:26:02 KST

Russian strikes on Ukraine kill at least 7, including woman at Kyiv's National Academy of Sciences
Kyiv, Ukraine — Russia's round-the-clock bombardment of targets in Ukraine killed at least seven people and wounded more than 50 others, officials said Monday.
Moscow's forces pounded apartment buildings, offices, data centers and a building of the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine in downtown Kyiv in a brazen daytime attack.
CBS News' Aidan Stretch was forced to take shelter again due to more incoming Russian weapons not long after he arrived Monday at the scene of the strike on the science academy.
The attacks followed a week of diplomatic efforts at the United Nations to get traction for negotiations on ending Moscow's full-scale invasion that began 4½ years ago.
Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov indicated Monday that the chances of making speedy headway on forging a peace settlement were bleak after recent Ukrainian attacks, including during recent parliamentary elections in Russia.
"Ukraine will have to pay a price for the actions that have taken place in recent months," Peskov told reporters. "That is happening right now."
On Saturday, Russian Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov said in a fiery speech to the U.N. General Assembly that "Europe is doing everything it can to thwart peace talks in which the Trump administration is interested," seeking, as Moscow has done throughout the war, to portray a rift within the NATO alliance.
Russian drone attacks across eastern Ukraine
Russian drone attacks on the Kyiv region killed four people and wounded eight, officials said.
A woman was killed in a Russian strike on Kyiv's Shevchenkivskyi district on Monday afternoon, the Kyiv city military administration said. The strike hit the National Academy of Sciences of Ukraine, the latest cultural landmark in the capital to be damaged. Russian forces also hit a pharmaceutical company and gas stations in Kyiv.
One drone struck an office center in central Dnipro during working hours Monday, killing three people and wounding at least 12, local authorities said.
A Russian strike on a nine-story apartment building in the northeast city of Kharkiv wounded 43 people, including 11 children, Mayor Ihor Terekhov said.
Four people, including two teenage girls, were hurt when a Russian drone struck a residential area in northern Ukraine's Chernihiv region on Sunday evening, said Viacheslav Chaus, head of the regional military administration.
Russia's Defense Ministry said its forces struck two data centers in Kyiv, as well as gas stations in the Ukrainian capital. A distribution hub belonging to the Nova Poshta postal service was struck in the southern city of Odesa, it said.
The Russian military also hit a cargo ship in the Black Sea and another one in the Ukrainian port of Chornomorsk, the ministry said. The strikes aim to curb Ukraine's grain exports, though they may also create food shortages in countries that rely on Ukrainian imports.
The Russian aerial attacks regularly hit civilian areas. Moscow claims it targets only military-related sites.
Ukraine claims small gains along entrenched front lines
Battlefield positions have changed little since last year, in part because swarms of drones severely restrict troop movements, but Kyiv's forces launched a recent offensive, code-named Operation Vivaldi, on part of the 800-mile front line.
Ukraine's Third Army Corps said Monday it had recaptured another 20 square miles from the Russians, bringing the total to 68 square miles since the offensive began several months ago.
The corps said that in order to break through Russian defenses, it converted Soviet-era BTR-60 armored personnel carriers into kamikaze vehicles that blew up the strongest Russian fortifications. The operation has also used ground robots to attack Russian positions.
The claimed breakthroughs came in the Donetsk region of eastern Ukraine, which the bigger Russian army has been trying in vain to conquer.
Russian officials made no immediate comment on the Ukrainian claim.
Russia's Defense Ministry, meanwhile, said Russian troops captured the villages of Novovodiane in the Donetsk region and Ulanove in the northern Sumy region.
It was not possible to independently verify the claims.
Zelenskyy said long-range strikes on Russian soil hit two defense plants in the Tula and Voronezh regions and oil facilities in the Krasnodar region, all in southern and western Russia.
Ukraine's long-range drones have repeatedly targeted Russian fuel depots and industrial plants that are a mainstay of Moscow's economy and war effort.
Ukrainian drone attacks overnight started fires at three infrastructure facilities in Russia's Krasnodar region, local emergency officials said Monday, without identifying the locations.
Russia's Defense Ministry said air defenses downed 254 Ukrainian drones overnight.
